research_question: What is the causal effect of cigarette smoking on the development of lung cancer?
background: Cigarette smoking is widely recognized as a major risk factor for lung cancer, but establishing causal inference in observational studies presents significant challenges. Smoking behavior is not randomly assigned and is strongly associated with numerous other risk factors including socioeconomic status, occupational exposures, and health behaviors. This framing addresses the methodological challenges of isolating the causal effect of smoking from confounding factors and selection bias inherent in epidemiological studies.

variables.name: smoking_exposure
variables.measurement: Pack-years calculated from smoking history questionnaires

variables.name: lung_cancer
variables.description: Diagnosis of primary lung cancer (ICD-10 C34)
variables.measurement: Medical records, cancer registry, or pathology reports

variables.name: age
variables.description: Age at study enrollment in years

variables.name: socioeconomic_status
variables.description: Socioeconomic status based on education and income

variables.name: alcohol_consumption
variables.description: Alcohol consumption in drinks per week

variables.name: genetic_risk_score
variables.description: Polygenic risk score for lung cancer susceptibility

variables.name: smoking_cessation_program
variables.description: Participation in smoking cessation program (potential instrument)

estimand.description: Average treatment effect of smoking on lung cancer risk in the target population
estimand.target_population: Adults aged 18+ in the general population

study_design.description: Prospective cohort study with retrospective smoking exposure assessment
study_design.assignment_mechanism: Natural assignment based on individual smoking behavior
study_design.data_collection_method: Baseline questionnaire with longitudinal follow-up through medical records

assumptions.name: Conditional Exchangeability
assumptions.description: Given measured covariates, smoking exposure is independent of potential lung cancer outcomes
assumptions.test_method: Balance tests after propensity score adjustment, negative control outcomes
assumptions.rationale: Core assumption for causal inference from observational data

assumptions.name: Positivity
assumptions.description: Every individual has non-zero probability of each smoking level given covariates
assumptions.test_method: Examination of propensity score distributions, overlap plots
assumptions.rationale: Ensures comparable groups for causal estimation

assumptions.name: Consistency
assumptions.description: Potential outcome under observed smoking exposure equals observed outcome
assumptions.test_method: Sensitivity analysis to different exposure definitions
assumptions.rationale: Links potential outcomes to observed data

assumptions.name: No Unmeasured Confounding
assumptions.description: All important confounders are measured and appropriately adjusted for

assumptions.name: Correct Model Specification
assumptions.description: Statistical models correctly specify relationships between variables

assumptions.name: No Selection Bias
assumptions.description: Study selection and loss to follow-up are independent of potential outcomes
assumptions.test_method: Compare characteristics of completers vs dropouts, inverse probability weighting
assumptions.rationale: Prevents biased estimates from selective participation

validation_criteria.name: Propensity Score Balance
validation_criteria.description: Covariates should be balanced across smoking groups after adjustment
validation_criteria.test: Love plots before and after adjustment

validation_criteria.name: Positivity Check
validation_criteria.description: Sufficient overlap in propensity scores across treatment groups

validation_criteria.name: Instrument Validity
validation_criteria.description: If using IV, instrument must satisfy relevance and exclusion restrictions

validation_criteria.name: Negative Control Test
validation_criteria.description: No effect should be found for outcomes that cannot be caused by smoking

validation_criteria.name: Sensitivity Analysis
validation_criteria.description: Estimates should be robust to reasonable unmeasured confounding

validation_criteria.name: Dose-Response Relationship
validation_criteria.description: Higher smoking exposure should lead to higher lung cancer risk

data_requirements.data_structure: Individual-level longitudinal cohort data with baseline exposure assessment and periodic outcome ascertainment

analysis_methods.name: Propensity Score Matching
analysis_methods.description: Match smokers and non-smokers on propensity scores
analysis_methods.limitations: Discards data, sensitive to model specification

analysis_methods.name: Inverse Probability Weighting
analysis_methods.description: Weight observations by inverse probability of treatment
analysis_methods.advantages: Uses full sample, estimates population ATE

analysis_methods.name: Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation
analysis_methods.description: Semiparametric efficient estimation with machine learning

analysis_methods.name: Instrumental Variables
analysis_methods.description: Use smoking cessation programs as instruments

limitations: Residual confounding from unmeasured factors (e.g., personality traits, stress)
Measurement error in smoking exposure assessment (recall bias)
Long latency period between smoking initiation and lung cancer development
Healthy smoker survivor bias in cross-sectional studies
Generalizability limited to populations with similar smoking patterns
Potential for selection bias due to differential loss to follow-up
Difficulty separating effects of different tobacco products
Changes in smoking behavior over time not captured in baseline assessment
ethical_considerations: Informed consent for long-term follow-up and genetic testing
Privacy protection for sensitive health and lifestyle information
Communication of individual risk findings to participants
Consideration of stigmatization in reporting smoking-related risks
Data sharing policies that protect participant confidentiality
